title: 10 things you need to know before building your first video game
summary: New to video game making? Learn the 10 design decisions to plan before you build – from core loop and scope to physics, camera, controls, and playtesting.
body_markdown:
### **8. Give every action feedback**


Every action needs a response the player can see or hear. Game makers call this “juice”: the little flashes, shakes, and sounds that make an action feel satisfying.[Research on how games feel](https://gala.gre.ac.uk/id/eprint/51671/) has focused on exactly this – controls that respond quickly, and feedback that’s a little exaggerated.


Juice doesn’t have to be fancy.[In one study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13695) , players liked comic-style sound words popping up onscreen, like “POW” or “BOOM,” about as much as bursts of sparks and debris.


Sound matters as much as visuals. It only takes a few seconds of playing your favorite game on mute to realize how important sound is. What’s on your screen counts as feedback too. A head-up display (HUD) – the health bar, score, or timer – needs as much planning as the rest of your game. Many games end up with weak on-screen displays because they’re treated as an afterthought.
